title: Finite cubical multiplication numerator calculation
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the coherent profinite site, $r\geq0$, $J$ a normalized comparison between generalized-section and discrete $\mathbf Z^r$ actions, $C$ a cubical model with the cell coproducts, boundary, translation and contraction of [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation], $K$ a finite subset-coordinate Koszul model [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and $B$ an equivariant unital $R$-algebra [lem-sfb-lattice-flat-twisted-chain-pairing]. Work in ordinary signed cochain tensors and derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $L=J(C.L)$, $X=tK(B)$ and $Z=B[0]$. Fix a subset-coordinate chain pairing $P$ as in [lem-sfb-lattice-flat-twisted-chain-pairing] and assume $B$ commutative. For every normalized roof datum $F$ of [def-sfb-lattice-cubical-multiplication-data], its multiplication numerators satisfy $f=\delta;g$, and its unit equation is $(tu\otimes1);E=\lambda;\varepsilon;\eta_B$. Moreover on the supported source summand indexed by degrees $p,q$, subsets $A,C$ and cell $[v,I]$, the first numerator has coefficient zero unless $A\cap C=\varnothing$ and $A\cup C=I$; otherwise it has coefficient $c_{p+q}\epsilon(A,C)T^v(x_A)T^{v+u_A}(y_C)$. No existence of F or denominator quasi-isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text:
Compute the first composite on a tensor supported in the summands $x_A\in K_B^p$, $y_C\in K_B^q$, with $|A|=p$, $|C|=q$, and on a cube $[v,I]$. The product formula contributes only if $A\cap C=\varnothing$ and $A\cup C=I$; evaluation also requires $|I|=p+q$. In that case it gives
$$c_{p+q}\epsilon(A,C)T^v\bigl(x_A T_A(y_C)\bigr)=c_{p+q}\epsilon(A,C)T^v(x_A)T^{v+u_A}(y_C).$$
Here the evaluation sign is $c_{p+q}$ because $B$ is in internal cochain degree zero. The equality uses $T_A=T^{u_A}$, commutation of the $T_i$ and multiplicativity of $T^v$. Otherwise it is zero. These are identities of internal bilinear maps: the supported summands and the free cube inclusions generate the source under coproducts and tensor products, so this calculation is not an assumption that sections generate every condensed module.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent lattice expansion: returned step 12; first numerator coefficient

proof.text:
For the second composite expand $\Delta[v,I]$. On the summands just used the two evaluations can be nonzero only for the unique partition $I=A\sqcup C$. The interchange of $y_C$ (degree $q$) and $[v,A]$ (degree $-p$) gives $(-1)^{-pq}=(-1)^{pq}$. Evaluation on the first cube gives $c_pT^v(x_A)$, and on the second gives $c_qT^{v+u_A}(y_C)$. Thus the coefficient is
$$\epsilon(A,C)(-1)^{pq}c_pc_q\,T^v(x_A)T^{v+u_A}(y_C).$$
Since
$$\frac{(p+q)(p+q+1)}2=\frac{p(p+1)}2+\frac{q(q+1)}2+pq,$$
this equals the coefficient in step 2 over every commutative $R$. If no such partition exists both coefficients are zero. Equality on the summand inclusions proves equality of the two chain maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent lattice expansion: returned step 12; second numerator and the sign identity

proof.text: For the unit, $tu$ has its only component in Koszul degree zero. Thus $E_B(tu\otimes1)$ is zero on cubes of positive dimension; on $[v,\varnothing]$ it is $c_0T^v(1_B)=1_B$. These are exactly the components of $\eta_B\varepsilon$, since $c_0=1$ and every $T_i$ fixes $1_B$.
